prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1140; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reports a collision at an intersection while the insured was turning left. Claimant states the other vehicle proceeded straight through a yellow light. Shoulder pain reported at scene. Claimant has not retained counsel and says they will handle the claim directly. Photos requested.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant describes right shoulder pain radiating into the upper arm, limited range of motion when reaching overhead. Claimant has been advised to seek medical evaluation and to keep all treatment records. Claimant confirmed no attorney involved at this time.

Entry 3: Reviewed police report. Officer notes the insured vehicle was turning left across oncoming traffic. Witness statement on file supports claimant's account of the signal phase. Liability appears to lean toward the insured, pending further review of scene photos and vehicle damage.

Entry 4: Claimant submitted medical documentation showing a diagnosis of rotator cuff strain and a referral for physical therapy. Claimant asked how the claim process works and whether a settlement offer will be made before treatment ends. Explained that a bodily injury evaluation generally waits until treatment is complete or stable.

Entry 5: Follow-up call with claimant. Claimant reports continued shoulder discomfort and is attending physical therapy twice weekly. Claimant still unrepresented and has not signed any release. Reminded claimant that a settlement decision will require full medical records and that we will keep them updated on status.
